text: {"claims":[{"cid":"c1","text":"A meta-regression of 16 UK minimum wage studies finds no overall practically significant adverse employment effect.","cited_pids":["5f591435f1d8#0"]},{"cid":"c2","text":"A meta-regression of UK minimum wage studies finds a possible genuine adverse employment effect in residential home care.","cited_pids":["5f591435f1d8#0"]},{"cid":"c3","text":"A review co-authored by Dube reports that most minimum wage studies find no job losses or only small disemployment effects.","cited_pids":["f3df8a818b8c#0"]},{"cid":"c4","text":"A synthesis of meta-analyses finds that corrected employment elasticities for minimum wages generally approach zero after accounting for publication bias.","cited_pids":["3ed11781c282#1"]},{"cid":"c5","text":"Research by Azar suggests the employment effect of minimum wages depends on labor market concentration.","cited_pids":["cb6fd29ac7f5#0"]},{"cid":"c6","text":"A Congressional Budget Office estimate for a $15 federal minimum wage projects about 1.4 million fewer jobs.","cited_pids":["6de9116294ca#3"]},{"cid":"c7","text":"A 1992 study found a 1–2% teen employment decline for every 10% increase in the minimum wage.","cited_pids":["ad8b67a3ca55#10"]},{"cid":"c8","text":"The Employment Policies Institute's critique of the New Jersey minimum wage study reported a 4.6% employment decline.","cited_pids":["9e1f48f1f498#3"]}]}
